floatingContract.leafTransform: raw binary32 sign-bit clear for every contributor
floatingContract.contributorOrder: strictly increasing source ordinal from zero through N-1
floatingContract.singleton: one direct raw ABS load/store and zero additions

siteInventory.operation: load_word followed by uint sign-bit clear and as_type<float>
siteInventory.proof: Each ordinal is loaded exactly once. Integer sign clearing is the exact raw ABS transform for zero, subnormal, normal, infinity, and NaN classes without payload truncation.

The loop starts at ordinal one, advances by one while below N, and assigns the sole safe-mode addition result to the only accumulator. Thus N leaves induce exactly N-1 actual additions and no zero leaf or parallel partial sum.
The final accumulator bits are stored once without numeric conversion, epsilon, finite substitution, or pre-truncation.

contributorProof.firstContributor: ordinal zero initializes accumulator from its raw ABS word
contributorProof.noDrop: There is no predicate, continue, finite-only branch, zero filter, or alternate update.
contributorProof.noSyntheticLeaf: No zero or identity accumulator is initialized.
contributorProof.noReassociation: One accumulator dependency chain, one output thread, one safe-mode addition site, and no reduction primitive fix the left-associated order.
contributorProof.singleton: N=1 bypasses the loop and stores the raw ABS word directly.

specialValueProof.zero: Raw ABS clears either input zero sign. Every later add is represented by the exact/RNE/DAZ/FTZ site relation; raw store preserves the device-selected permitted result bits.
specialValueProof.subnormal: A raw ABS leaf remains exact. At an addition site each subnormal operand is exact or same-sign zero under DAZ, and each subnormal rounded result is exact or same-sign zero under FTZ; the Lean relation admits no third choice.
specialValueProof.normal: Every finite normal contributor enters exactly one ordinal addition, and no source branch filters, rescales, or truncates it.
specialValueProof.infinity: ABS maps either infinity sign to positive infinity. Safe binary32 addition with non-NaN nonnegative contributors retains positive-infinity class; finite overflow may also publish positive infinity.
specialValueProof.nan: ABS preserves exponent and payload fields while clearing only sign. N=1 stores those raw bits directly; an N>1 safe addition publishes NaN class without a finite fallback.
specialValueProof.daz: The formal primitive relation enumerates exact input or same-sign zero only for a subnormal input.
specialValueProof.ftz: The formal primitive relation enumerates exact rounded output or same-sign zero only for a subnormal rounded output.

formalProofBoundary.proved: Total raw classes, exact ABS class/sign behavior, complete set-valued DAZ/FTZ alternatives, labelled contributor multiplicity, permitted left tree, N-1 add nodes, N=1 direct ABS, and source-fold membership in the Model result set.
formalProofBoundary.primitivePremise: The single hardware addition is an RNE binary32 site with only the enumerated DAZ/FTZ alternatives; the audited MTLMathModeSafe/MTLLanguageVersion3_2 runtime site and compiled AIR source site supply this premise.
formalProofBoundary.forbiddenAssumptions: Both Lean files compile without sorry or axiom declarations.
